title: The Hollows
text: Oval caverns in the crust, a few meters across, their walls grown over with quartz and amethyst, emerald in the deeper ones. Each has a pool at the bottom: fresh water at 37 C, level no matter how the rock around it tilts. No two hollows connect, yet their pools rise and fall together, a few millimeters, about once a minute. Some hold a lamp on a ledge and someone beside it who will trade. They never say how they got in. Writers of the 1800s described a hidden country under the crust, Agartha, reached by doors few could find. Asked about Agartha, the traders only ask what you are buying.
teaser: The pools rise and fall together, about once a minute.
